questions.question: What color are the pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines are used in the center of the road to separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: Drivers age 21 or older cannot drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs indicate?
questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs show you are in a school zone. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians near schools.

questions.question: You must yield to other drivers:

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on a road to your left and you have reached an unmarked intersection at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, turn your steering wheel:

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, turn the steering wheel in the direction you want it to go. Once the vehicle straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, a pedestrian should walk on the:

options.text: Side of the road which has the lightest traffic.
Same side of the road on which traffic is moving.
Side of the road facing oncoming traffic.
Side of the road which has the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side of the road facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing the traffic in the nearest lane.

questions.question: Unless posted otherwise, the maximum speed limit on a dirt or gravel road is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 55 mph.
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit on a dirt or gravel road is 55 miles per hour under normal conditions. Always follow posted speed limits if they are different.

questions.question: Which of the following is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Maintain a constant speed throughout the curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve and gradually increase your speed as you exit. Speeding up as you enter a curve makes it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop at a yield sign if traffic requires it.

questions.question: When visibility is reduced, your first response should be:

options.text: Looking for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reducing your speed.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed when visibility decreases or road conditions are dangerous.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The driver on the left can go when it is safe.

questions.question: You cannot park within ____ feet of a crosswalk or intersection.
questions.explanation: You cannot park within 10 feet of a crosswalk or intersection. There are many places where parking is not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be in the area.

questions.question: If an oncoming vehicle is heading toward you in your lane, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn, steer right, and speed up.
Honk your horn, steer left, and brake.
Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk your horn, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: If another vehicle is coming straight at you, honk your horn first to get their attention. If they do not move, steer to the right. Do not steer left because the other driver may correct at the last second and you will still crash. If a crash cannot be avoided, brake hard and steady. Each mile per hour slower will reduce the damage from the crash.

questions.question: The most important thing to remember about speed and curves is that you must:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit when you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: You must slow down before entering a curve. Your vehicle's momentum may make it hard to turn, so you need to reduce speed to stay in control.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Stop next to the front car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop next to the front car.
questions.explanation: After you find a spot, check traffic, and signal, stop parallel to the car in front of the empty space. Then turn your wheels to park.

questions.question: What do regulatory signs do?

options.text: They are placed everywhere there is danger.
They tell you what you must or must not do.
They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell you what you must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black writing on white. They tell you what you must or must not do. They show speed limits, no passing zones, no turns, and other rules.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is starting. The road will split into two separate one-way roads with a median between them. You must stay on the right side.

questions.question: Which statement about work zones is true?

options.text: They can be moving or stationary.
They are marked with black and white signs.
You do not need to slow down or pay extra attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving, such as machines for striping, mowing, or removing snow. Work zones have orange signs with black letters. Slow down and stay alert when you see or drive through a work zone.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign is a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow. In work areas, they are orange. These signs warn you that there is a hazard ahead or special rules apply.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a roundabout?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you approach a roundabout. Roundabouts are designed to be driven at low speeds.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to the lane you came from.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the lane you came from.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you came from. This keeps your turn safe and smooth.

questions.question: What are crosswalks?

options.text: Always marked with horizontal lines on the road.
Always marked with vertical lines on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Marked with lines or unmarked.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks can be marked or unmarked. Either way, you must stop and let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: Which does NOT affect how far it takes to stop your vehicle?

options.text: How far the brakes take to work.
How far you travel while reacting.
How long it takes you to notice danger.

questions.correctAnswerText: How well you can steer.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on how long it takes you to notice danger, how far you travel while reacting, and how far the brakes take to work. These change based on speed and road conditions.

questions.question: What should drivers do when using a roundabout?

options.text: Let cars already in the roundabout go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let cars already in the roundabout go first.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection with no traffic light. Traffic moves counterclockwise around a center island. When entering, you must yield to cars already in the roundabout. Then drive around the circle until you reach your exit.
